title: UP's draft voter roll lists 13.58 crore, up 18.84 lakh; SP alleges a plan to add fake voters
dek: Uttar Pradesh's election office published the draft roll for the 2027 Assembly election on Tuesday. Akhilesh Yadav says his party will watch every new name; the BJP accuses him of threatening officials.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Uttar Pradesh's draft electoral roll for the 2027 Assembly election lists 13.58 crore voters, a net increase of 18.84 lakh over the final roll published on 10 April after this year's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the state's Chief Electoral Officer, Navdeep Rinwa, said on Tuesday, 17 November. Voters now have until 16 December to apply to be added, to object to names, or to correct their entries.

The draft, delayed by five days from 12 November, has set off a new round in the fight between the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Samajwadi Party (SP). SP president Akhilesh Yadav alleged that the BJP would try to get fake voters enrolled through Form 6, the form for new voters, and said his party would track every addition, according to reports. The BJP's state president, Pankaj Chaudhary, accused him of threatening officials, reports said.

## What the draft shows

According to the figures released by the Chief Electoral Officer, the draft has 7.38 crore men, 6.20 crore women and 4,042 third-gender electors. Reports differ slightly on the number of men; one gives 7.39 crore. Nearly 11 lakh women and about 7.87 lakh men were added since April, while the number of third-gender voters fell by 164, according to reports.

The number of voters aged 18 and 19 is 11.83 lakh, down from 17.63 lakh in the April roll, according to reports.

The roll can be checked at 1,73,730 polling booths across 403 Assembly constituencies in 75 districts, or online on the Chief Electoral Officer's portal using a voter ID (EPIC) number, mobile number or personal details. Citizens who turn 18 by 1 January 2027 can apply.

## Questions over who is missing

Population projections estimate about 16.16 crore citizens aged 18 or over in the state, which would leave around 2.58 crore people missing from the draft, according to reports. The projections suggest 7.84 crore eligible women, against 6.20 crore on the roll, and 84.47 lakh people aged 18 or 19, against 11.83 lakh enrolled. Officials said a statistical gap of this kind should not be read as a count of eligible voters left out, reports said.

Asked about criticism that the SIR had disenfranchised voters, especially women and young people, Mr Rinwa said: "Now we are trying to enfranchise the people," according to reports. He warned that holding a voter ID card "does not necessarily mean a person's name is still on the electoral roll", and said the aim was "to ensure that by January 4, there is not a single duplicate entry". Action under Sections 31 and 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, would be taken against anyone enrolling fake voters and against officials involved in irregularities, he said.

Last week the election office told voters who had been on the rolls before the SIR but were dropped from it that they could apply again on Form 6 without facing prosecution, provided they were not registered elsewhere.

## What the parties say

Mr Yadav said the SP had set up a monitoring system of booth in-charges, party workers and supporters to check new additions, and that if a name was added improperly the party would file a complaint against the officer responsible and seek action, according to reports. He also accused the BJP of using the category of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate voters to manipulate the roll.

Mr Chaudhary said the SP chief had not changed despite ten years out of power, and accused him of trying to intimidate officials doing their duty, reports said.

The row follows Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's claim that 1.27 crore Hindu voters are missing from the rolls, which the SP disputed.

## What happens next

- 17 November to 16 December: claims and objections on Forms 6 (new voters), 7 (deletions) and 8 (corrections).
- 28 December: last date for deciding claims and objections.
- 4 January 2027: final roll published.

The Election Commission's handling of the SIR is also before the Supreme Court, where opposition parties have challenged deletions and the Commission has said voters who were dropped and reapply will not be prosecuted.
